en: So at this point, we had a very close look
at how we can configure the requests that
are sent and managed by HTMX.
But it turns out that we can actually also
configure the responses quite a bit and with
them
also change the behavior of HTMX. And that's
what I'll show you next.
And I wanna start with submitting the form.
When we submit the form,
we of course send this POST request to
/login.
Now,
in that login route, we're then validating
the inputs and you already saw what happens
if an invalid input is entered.
But if we succeed, I'm currently not sending
back anything. I'm sending back an empty
response.
Now, what we might wanna do
if we're facing a login form like this
is that when the user enters valid
credentials
and we click login,
we might want to redirect the user to a new
page.
So we might want to redirect to
/authenticated here, for example, so to this
route.
Now, of course, if you recall what you
learned in earlier sections,
we'll have a problem if we try to do that.
So here, if I
reload and I enter a valid email
and then some valid password and I click
login,
you see the content of the next page is
rendered here.
It's rendered on the existing page. And that
happens because, as you learned, HTMX by
default follows redirects like this.
And therefore, as a result, we
don't load a new page in the browser, but
instead HTMX gets the response of that new
page or of this GET route here to be
precise.
And it then renders that into the target of
the request we sent, so into this target
here.
Now, that sometimes is the behavior you
want,
but sometimes you might want a real
redirect.
And you can achieve that and change the
behavior of HTMX by setting a specific
header on the response.
And here in Node, when using Express.js, you
can do that by calling the setHeader header
method on that response object before
sending it.
And the header I wanna set here
is one of the special headers you can set on
the responses that are sent back and that
will be handled by HTMX.
Specifically, you can set the hx-redirect
response header to
really trigger a client-side redirect to a
new page.
So to not have HTMX take the response and
render it into the target, but to really
instead perform a redirect.
And you see some other response headers and
what they do here as well, but I'll get back
to some of them later. For the moment, let's
focus on that redirect header.
So here it's HX-Redirect, which I wanna set,
and I wanna set that to /authenticated.
And this will then ensure that we indeed do
redirect the user to that page and that that
new page is therefore loaded
and that HTMX will not just take the content
of that page and render it somewhere else.
Now, one thing you'll need to do though is
you should then not also send such a
redirect response here, but instead just
send an empty response.
But with that, if you save everything,
if you reload here
and you enter some
valid credentials and you click login,
you see now I'm really redirected to a new
page. We completely replaced the existing
page with this one.
And of course I can still go back and forth
now with the back and forward buttons.
And that's the case because we now really
redirected the user.
